Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 1) The greenhouse gas with the highest relative contribution mentioned is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Carbon dioxide contributes about 76% to greenhouse effect. It is the most abundant important greenhouse gas. Methane and nitrous oxide contribute less.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 2) Methane contributes approximately:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Methane contributes about 16% to greenhouse effect. It is less abundant than carbon dioxide. But it is an important greenhouse gas.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 3) Nitrous oxide contributes approximately:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Nitrous oxide contributes about 6%. It has less contribution than carbon dioxide and methane. It still plays an important role in global warming.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 4) Which greenhouse gas is natural and amplifies warming?
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Water vapor is a natural greenhouse gas. It amplifies warming. It is different from man-made pollutants like CFCs.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 5) CFCs are best described as:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.option1: Potent but less abundant greenhouse gases
Environment, Noise, Radiation.option3: Most abundant but weak greenhouse gases
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: CFCs are potent greenhouse gases. They are less abundant compared with carbon dioxide. They are also important in ozone depletion.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 6) Ground-level ozone has:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Ozone has a minor role at ground level in greenhouse effect. It is not the major contributor. Carbon dioxide has the largest contribution.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 7) Kyoto Protocol is mainly related to:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.option3: Global commitment to limit warming below 2°C
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Kyoto Protocol deals with greenhouse gas reduction. It is legally binding. It is different from Montreal Protocol and Paris Agreement.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 8) Paris Agreement was adopted in:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Paris Agreement was adopted in 2015. It aims to limit global warming. The target mentioned is below 2°C.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 9) Paris Agreement mainly aims to limit warming to:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Paris Agreement is a global climate commitment. It aims to limit warming below 2°C. It has a broader global participation approach.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 10) Montreal Protocol mainly controls:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.option2: Greenhouse gas emission from factories only
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Montreal Protocol controls ozone-depleting substances. CFCs are the classic example. It is different from Kyoto Protocol.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 11) CFC control is mainly associated with:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Montreal Protocol controls CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances. CFCs damage the ozone layer. This is a common environmental health recall point.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 12) X-rays and gamma rays are examples of:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: X-rays and gamma rays are ionizing radiation. They have high penetration. They can damage DNA and increase cancer risk.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 13) Alpha and beta particles are classified as:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Alpha and beta particles are ionizing radiation. They can produce ionization in tissues. Ionizing radiation can cause mutations and cancer.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 14) UV rays, microwaves and radio waves are examples of:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: UV rays, microwaves and radio waves are non-ionizing radiation. They have lower penetration than X-rays and gamma rays. They may cause burns, cataract and thermal injury.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 15) The major health hazard of ionizing radiation is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Ionizing radiation can damage DNA. It may cause cancer and mutations. This makes radiation protection essential.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 16) Health effects of non-ionizing radiation include:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Non-ionizing radiation has lower penetration. It can still cause burns and cataract. Microwave exposure may cause thermal injury.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 17) Immediate somatic effect of radiation includes:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Radiation sickness is an immediate somatic effect. It is also called acute radiation syndrome. Delayed effects appear later.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 18) Acute radiation syndrome is classified as:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Acute radiation syndrome occurs soon after significant exposure. It is an immediate somatic effect. Delayed somatic effects include leukaemia and carcinogenesis.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 19) Leukaemia after radiation exposure is a:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Leukaemia is a delayed somatic effect of radiation. Carcinogenesis and fetal developmental abnormalities are also delayed effects. They may appear long after exposure.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 20) Chromosome mutation due to radiation is a:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Chromosome mutation is a genetic effect of radiation. Point mutations are also included. Genetic effects may affect future generations.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 21) Point mutation due to radiation is classified as:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Point mutation is a genetic effect. It involves alteration in genetic material. Radiation protection reduces both somatic and genetic risks.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 22) Basic principles of radiation protection include time, distance and:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Radiation protection depends on time, distance and shielding. Exposure time should be minimized. Lead apron and barriers are examples of shielding.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 23) Minimizing exposure duration represents which radiation protection principle?
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Shorter exposure duration reduces radiation dose. This is the time principle. It is one of the three basic protection methods.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 24) Standing as far as possible from radiation represents:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Increasing distance reduces exposure. Radiation intensity falls as distance increases. This is a basic radiation safety principle.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 25) Use of lead apron in radiation work is an example of:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Lead apron provides shielding. It blocks or reduces radiation reaching the body. Barriers are also used for shielding.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 26) Chernobyl nuclear disaster occurred in:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Chernobyl occurred in Ukraine in 1986. It was a nuclear reactor disaster. It is an important radiation incident.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 27) Fukushima disaster occurred in:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Fukushima occurred in Japan in 2011. It followed an earthquake-triggered nuclear disaster. It is an important modern radiation incident.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 28) Hiroshima and Nagasaki are associated with:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Hiroshima and Nagasaki were affected by atomic bombs in 1945. They are classical examples of radiation effects. The consequences included acute and long-term health effects.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 29) Air Quality Index is usually expressed on a scale of:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Air Quality Index categorizes air pollution on a 0–500 scale. Higher values indicate worse air quality. It helps communicate pollution risk to the public.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 30) PM2.5 refers to particulate matter less than:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: PM2.5 means fine particles below 2.5 microns. It is especially harmful to health. Smaller particles can enter deeper into the lungs.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 31) The most harmful particulate indicator mentioned is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: PM2.5 is described as the most harmful particulate matter indicator. It is fine enough to penetrate deep into lungs. It is more dangerous than larger particles.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 32) WHO annual mean limit for PM2.5 mentioned is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: PM2.5 annual mean limit is mentioned as below 5 microgram/m³. This reflects strict air quality protection. Higher levels increase respiratory and cardiovascular risk.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 33) PM10 refers to particles smaller than:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: PM10 means particles smaller than 10 microns. They can enter the respiratory tract. PM2.5 is finer and generally more harmful.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 34) Residential area daytime noise limit is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Residential daytime noise limit is ≤55 dB. At night the limit is lower. Noise control protects sleep and mental health.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 35) Residential area nighttime noise limit is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Residential nighttime noise limit is ≤45 dB. It is lower than daytime limit. Night noise disturbs sleep and recovery.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 36) Industrial area noise limit is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Industrial area noise limit is ≤75 dB. This is higher than residential and silence zones. Industrial areas usually tolerate more noise.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 37) Silence zone daytime noise limit near hospitals and schools is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Silence zone daytime limit is ≤50 dB. Hospitals and schools need quieter surroundings. Nighttime limit is even lower.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 38) Silence zone nighttime noise limit is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Silence zone nighttime limit is ≤40 dB. This protects sleep, recovery and learning environments. It is stricter than residential nighttime limit.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 39) Auditory effect of noise pollution includes:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Noise pollution can cause hearing loss and tinnitus. These are auditory effects. Long-term exposure increases risk.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 40) Cardiovascular effect of noise pollution includes:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Noise pollution can increase blood pressure. Hypertension and increased heart rate are cardiovascular effects. Noise acts as a chronic stressor.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 41) Psychological effects of noise pollution include:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Noise pollution affects mental well-being. Irritability, anxiety and sleep disturbance are listed psychological effects. Sleep disturbance also worsens daytime performance.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 42) Cognitive effect of noise pollution is especially important in:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Noise can reduce attention and learning. This is especially important in children. Schools need quieter surroundings for effective learning.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 43) General effects of noise pollution include:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Noise pollution may cause headache and fatigue. Stress is another general effect. These effects reduce comfort and productivity.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 44) The major outdoor air pollutant related to incomplete combustion and impaired oxygen transport is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Carbon monoxide is produced by incomplete combustion. It binds strongly with hemoglobin and reduces oxygen transport. This may cause headache, dizziness and even death in severe exposure. Poor ventilation increases the risk of poisoning.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 45) Photochemical smog is mainly associated with:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.option3: Cold humid weather and smoke only
Environment, Noise, Radiation.option4: Sunlight acting on nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Photochemical smog forms when sunlight acts on nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons. It is common in traffic-polluted urban areas. Ozone and other oxidants are important components. It irritates eyes and respiratory tract.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 46) Classical London smog is mainly associated with:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Classical London smog is reducing smog. It is associated with smoke, fog and sulfur dioxide, especially from coal burning. It occurs more in cold, damp conditions. It causes respiratory morbidity and excess mortality.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 47) Ozone layer depletion mainly increases exposure to:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: The ozone layer absorbs much of the harmful ultraviolet radiation. Depletion allows more UV radiation to reach earth. This increases risk of skin cancer, cataract and immune effects. CFC control helps protect the ozone layer.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 48) The most radiosensitive cells are generally:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Rapidly dividing cells are more radiosensitive. Bone marrow, gonads and intestinal mucosa are important examples. Radiation damages DNA, so cells undergoing division are more vulnerable. This explains marrow suppression and reproductive effects after exposure.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 49) The first principle in controlling air pollution is usually:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.option1: Treatment of all exposed persons only
Environment, Noise, Radiation.option4: Control at the origin of pollution
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Air pollution control is most effective when pollutants are reduced at origin. This includes cleaner fuel, emission control and industrial regulation. Dispersion and personal protection are secondary measures. Prevention is better than treating health effects after exposure.

Environment, Noise, Radiation.question: 50) The best long-term prevention of noise-induced hearing loss is:
Environment, Noise, Radiation.option3: Reducing exposure by engineering and personal protection
Environment, Noise, Radiation.exp: Noise-induced hearing loss is preventable. Engineering control, machine maintenance, enclosure and ear protection reduce exposure. Limiting duration of exposure is also important. Once permanent hearing loss occurs, it may not fully recover.
